category_title: Secondary PRU students with low self-worth and mainstream avoidance
scenario_title: Navigating perceived pressure and behavioral expectations in mainstream versus alternative provision
minimal_context: The tutor is asking the student to complete a GCSE practice paper in a mainstream classroom setting.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to complete this GCSE practice paper today. It is important to finish this so you can prepare for your exams.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I know you need GCSEs to get to go to a good college to get a career. But the school wanting that good reputation so choosing the normal kids... but then the people that are below that standard are like the outcasts...

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's just focus on the questions in front of you right now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: If you can get through mainstream then [sighs] congratulations basically... You either deal with it or you don't... I had to back away, it was too much.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to keep working. I heard about the incident in the hallway earlier, and you need to show you can behave and finish this assignment.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: She pushed me over so I punched her in the face! You're always blaming me. The school's corrupt... They got me excluded... The internal exclusion happened... I can't avoid it...
